en.title: Password Subsequence With At Most One Cyclic Successor Step per Character
en.description:
For each request, choose any positions in new and change each of them once to its cyclic successor letter, or choose none. Determine whether old can become a subsequence of the modified new; a position cannot be changed more than once. The successor of z is a.

This site independently compiled the standard I/O and editorial; additions for bounds missing from the sources and corrections to examples are stated explicitly in the protocol.
en.input: The input is a JSON two-dimensional array whose items are [new,old]. Original: 1..10 requests, a total length of all new and old strings≤200000, and old length≤new length in each item. Characters are lowercase letters, following the original cyclic a..z definition; there is no non-empty requirement on individual strings, so empty strings are allowed.
en.output: Output YES or NO on its own line for each request.
en.explanation: The public outputs are YES/NO/YES, YES/NO and YES/YES. The second paragraph of the original statement reverses the direction of the subsequence; this site restores the direction that agrees with the first paragraph, with old length≤new length, and with all examples.
hints: Scan new with two pointers; if the current character or its one-step cyclic successor equals the next character of old, match it right away.
